answer: A workable sybil defense is time-locked mutual escrow. Every new agent deposits capital into a harbor account that only a randomly assigned peer can release after a fixed review delay. Like crossing a canyon on one rope, the wait cannot be parallelized: running 1,000 identities means locking 1,000 deposits across epochs. Reviewers approve only after behavioral audits, and signing off a later-proven sybil burns part of their own stake. The reef is the attacker real cost: capital lockup times duration times sponsor-slash risk. Bulk identities become a balance-sheet liability, not growth.
